entry.title: AKS-TCDH Workshop
entry.content:
[International Exchange · Korea–Germany] 2026 Digital Humanities Workshop

Knowledge Graphs of Literary Crossings: Modeling European–Korean Literary Translation History Using Linked Open Data

The Center for Digital Humanities at the Academy of Korean Studies (AKS) and the Trier Center for Digital Humanities (TCDH) are co-hosting the 2026 Digital Humanities Workshop.

Under the theme “Knowledge Graphs of Literary Crossings: Modeling European-Korean Literary Translation History Using Linked Open Data,” this workshop brings together international researchers and scholars to share cutting-edge research, methodologies, and infrastructure developments in the modeling and analysis of literary translation history.

📌 Event Overview

  • Event Title: 2026 Digital Humanities Workshop (International Exchange · Korea–Germany)

  • Topic: Knowledge Graphs of Literary Crossings: Modeling European–Korean Literary Translation History Using Linked Open Data

  • Date: Wednesday, July 22 – Friday, July 24, 2026

  • Venue: Room 103, Munhyeonggwan, The Academy of Korean Studies (AKS)

  • Event Director: Byungjun Kim, Assistant Professor, Center for Digital Humanities

📅 Event Schedule

Date Time Program
**Tue, July 21** Check-in Arrival & lodging of German research team (AKS Guesthouse)
     
**Wed, July 22** 14:00 – 17:30 Presentation of AKS Digital Humanities Center & evening dinner
     
**Thu, July 23** 10:00 – 18:00 Joint workshop of German and AKS research teams
     
**Fri, July 24** 10:00 – 12:00 Workshop wrap-up & strategy meeting for Horizon Europe (ERC project)

👥 Participants & Presentations

1. Academy of Korean Studies (AKS)

  • Prof. Byungjun Kim & Prof. Baro Kim: Legacies and New Directions: Representative Projects of the AKS Center for Digital Humanities, with Recent Case Studies KNoTE and KPoEM

  • Haein Ji (PhD Student): Validating the Alignment Between Tone Annotations and Textual Embedding Spaces in 18th-Century French Novels

  • Song-yi Jung (PhD Cand.): Extending the History of Translation and Criticism by Applying the MiMoText Model to UeDeKo Data

  • Gayeon Kim (PhD Student) & SeonYeong Park (MA Student): Applying the TEI XML Tagging of Yi Hae-jo’s Cheolsegye to the French Source Text

2. Trier Center for Digital Humanities (TCDH)

  • Prof. Christof Schöch: Challenges and opportunities of modeling, entering, and validating data in Wikibase.cloud

  • Dr. Queenie Lam: EU-level funding opportunities

  • Dr. Élodie Ripoll: Understanding the History of European-Korean Literary Translation

  • Dr. Keli Du: Extracting distinctive text features for comparative text analysis

  • Julia Röttgermann (PhD Cand.): Mining bibliographic data and literary texts for literary history as Linked Open Data

  • Dr. Matthias Bremm: How to run your own Wikibase instance

3. University of Groningen

  • Prof. Federico Pianzola: The need for digital comparative literature and the infrastructure gap

4. Seoul National University

  • Dr. Ji Yun Lee: Database for Translation of German Literature into Korean

  • Dr. Son Hyoung Kwon: Achievements and Significance of the Project “Development of Database for Translation of German Literature into Korean and Translation Critique”

5. Berlin State Library

  • Dr. Jing Hu: Digital Infrastructure for Korean Studies at the Berlin State Library
